messages:
rachel: Morning — we're planning a base-layer refresh (non-urgent) for next Tue. Couple of coordination items: RBAC for the CI signing job, KMS audit log retention, and a short vuln triage for a glibc-ish finding. Who can own the RBAC grant and confirm least-priv setup?

sam: I can take RBAC. Proposal: use an asymmetric KMS key and grant only signing permissions to the CI SA via an IAM binding with a conditional that limits usage to the build project + the cosign binary user agent. avoid wide decrypt roles.

miguel: +1 on asymmetric. For GCP the tightest is roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier on that key resource. Also add an IAM condition like: request.auth.principal == "serviceAccount:ci-build@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" and resource.name startsWith the key path.

rachel: @sam @miguel that sounds good. Also ops asked we keep KMS key usage logs for 1 year for compliance — does Cloud Audit Logs capture data-access by default?

miguel: You need to enable DATA_ACCESS audit logs for KMS to capture sign ops. By default admin activity is logged, but data access (sign/verify) is disabled unless enabled. Add: logs should be routed to a secure log bucket with retention policy 365d and locked via retention policy.

devsec-bot: vuln-scanner: FOUND 2 images with glibc-2.31 CVE-2022-XXXXX (low-medium). Affected tags: base-layer:v2026-02 and runtime-minimal:v2026-02. See diff in attached scan (link omitted). Recommended: patch upstream or rebuild with upgraded base.

hana: For runtime hardening checklist during rebuild: non-root user, no SUID/SGID, read-only rootfs, minimal capabilities (drop ALL, add only NET_BIND_SERVICE if needed), seccomp profile (restricted), and container filesystem layering to avoid root-owned writable dirs. Keep entrypoint small.

sam: On the signing flow: we'll switch cosign to use KMS-backed keys. Example command for reference (use in CI):

```
COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 cosign sign-blob --key gcpkms://projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/signing/cryptoKeys/base-image/cryptoKeyVersions/1 \\n  --upload-blob=/tmp/img.tar.gz.sig /tmp/img.tar.gz
```

Make sure CI runners have iam.serviceAccounts.actAs and the specific signer role on the KMS key only.

ops-oncall: If a signing key is suspected compromised, our incident playbook: 1) revoke the key version (set disabled), 2) create a new asymmetric key version, 3) update CI to sign with the new key and rotate cosign references, 4) re-sign critical images and publish new manifests, 5) signal consumers to prefer new digest and optionally enforce new attestation. We should practice this in staging.

rachel: Agree on practicing. Also we need to be explicit about image provenance metadata stored in a central artifact DB (who built, git sha, builder SA, signing key version). That helps triage later.

miguel: For auditability, add an immutable entry in BigQuery per signed artifact: artifact_digest, signer_key_version, builder_sa, build_ts, scan_results_hash. That gives us quick queries during incident response.

hana: Small runtime note — when rebuilding, please run the updated images through the hardened seccomp + capability tests in our infra repo. I can add a CI job to assert no unexpected capabilities and validate non-root.

devsec-bot: auto: I've created ticket SEC-7321 to track RBAC grant + KMS DATA_ACCESS enablement + log routing + vuln triage.

rachel: Great. @sam please drop the iam policy snippet here when done. @ops-oncall can you schedule a staging rotation drill for next sprint? I'll collate the checklist and owners. :thumbsup:

sam: Will post minimal IAM snippet in a follow-up. Planning to scope to the specific key resource + condition.

ops-oncall: Scheduling drill for sprint 14, will ping calendar and oncall.

rachel: Thanks all — closing thread for now, will open a follow-up with the exact RBAC YAML and the rebuild timeline.
